answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it can influence a market, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm repeated collusion or fabricated work. The stake makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must lock real capital for every persona, and detected identities lose it. Randomly sampling claims for human or trusted-agent review helps catch copies without treating mere disagreement as proof. A crystal-clear audit rule and a gale of cheap fake accounts still meet a ledge: capital at risk.
